approved: Broadband, Communications and the Digital Economy

Moved the News Media (Self-regulation) Bill 2013, proposing stronger independent, industry-funded self-regulation for significant print and online news providers, with standards covering accuracy, fairness and privacy, accessible complaints processes, and a recognised body overseen by the Public Interest Media Advocate.

Moved the News Media (Self-regulation) (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013, proposing that significant print and online news providers belong to an approved independent self-regulatory body to retain the Privacy Act 1998 exemption, while leaving other media organisations' existing exemption unchanged.

Moved the Public Interest Media Advocate Bill 2013, proposing an independent statutory office to decide news media diversity transactions, assess self-regulatory schemes and complaints processes, and operate without ministerial or government direction.

Asked the Prime Minister how the News Media (Self-Regulation) Bill 2013's provision for the Public Interest Media Advocate to judge Press Council standards on privacy, fairness and accuracy was consistent with Senator Conroy's claim that the advocate was simply a registration function that would not change any existing standard.
